asks: how do I play Amumu
what's Amumu supposed to do
what does my champ want this game
how do I win as Amumu
say: You're an engage tank: farm to six, then open fights with Bandage Toss into your ultimate, or peel your carry if their divers are fed.
more: Before your ultimate you bring one stun and not much else, so the early game is about staying even on camps rather than forcing plays.
After six every objective fight starts on your terms, because Curse of the Sad Mummy stuns everyone standing near you.
Late, your job narrows to one question each fight: go in on their carries, or stand next to yours and stun whoever jumps on them.
check: Whether your team has damage that can follow your stun, and whether Flash is ready for the engage.
breaks: If you're far behind in levels, stop leading fights; stay beside your carry and use the stun on whoever dives.

asks: what's my first clear on Amumu
do I full clear or gank early
how should I path as Amumu
farm or gank first
say: Full clear and end beside the lane that has a stun to chain with your bandage, or stop at three camps if that lane's already fighting.
more: Despair and Tantrum both hit everything around you, and Tantrum comes back faster each time you're hit, so camps with several monsters go down quickly.
A full clear is about level four, which gives you all three basic abilities ranked for the first gank and the crab fight at 2:55.
You lean toward farming early because your real power is the ultimate, and each camp you skip pushes level six later.
check: Which lane is pushed toward your side, and whether your laner there has crowd control of their own.
breaks: If their jungler shows on the far side early, you can take the nearer crab for free instead of forcing a gank.

asks: who do I gank as Amumu
which lane should I gank before six
is it worth ganking right now
should I gank or keep farming
say: Gank the lane with a stun or slow to cover a missed bandage, or keep farming toward six if every lane is pushed up.
more: Before six, Bandage Toss is your only way in, so the gank is decided by that one skillshot unless your laner can hold them first.
Coming from behind or the side of the wave matters, because minions will block the bandage if you throw it through the wave.
A failed gank costs you about a camp of time, and you're a champion who would rather hit six on schedule.
check: Where the wave is in that lane, and whether minions stand between you and the target.
breaks: If the enemy laner still has their dash or Flash, a lone bandage rarely lands; farm, or wait until your laner starts the fight.

asks: when am I strong on Amumu
what's my power spike
I just hit six what now
when should I start fighting
say: Level six is your spike: gank a lane where two enemies stand together, or set up dragon if your bot lane has priority.
more: Your ultimate stuns and curses everyone near you, so it's worth far more on two or three targets than on one.
The Curse makes enemies take extra true damage from magic damage, so the spike is bigger when your laners deal magic damage.
If their jungler is still level five when you hit six, the next few minutes are your window to pick the fight at an objective.
check: Whether the lane you want has both enemies close together, and whether your ultimate is actually ready.
breaks: If you already used the ultimate and it's still down, you're back to a one-stun champion; farm or cover a lane until it returns.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Amumu
who do I ult
do I go in or peel
when do I engage on Amumu
say: Bandage onto their backline and ult when several are close, or hold the ultimate to stop their dive if your carry is the win condition.
more: Going in works when your team is close enough to follow within a second or two; otherwise you stun three people and nothing happens.
Holding it flips the fight the other way: their divers commit onto your carry, you stun all of them, and your carry gets free damage.
Stand in the middle once you're in, because Despair drains health from everyone near you and Tantrum keeps resetting as they hit you.
check: How far your team is behind you, and whether their carries are grouped or spread out.
breaks: If their team is spread wide, don't fish for a big ultimate; use it on the one fed carry you can reach, or save it to peel.

asks: how do I play Caitlyn
what does Caitlyn want
what's my game plan on Cait
how do I win as Caitlyn
say: Use your range to bully lane and take the tower early, or farm safely toward crit items if their lane can jump on you.
more: Caitlyn's strength is attacking from farther away than most marksmen, so the lane is yours whenever the enemy has no way to reach you.
An early tower lets you move to another lane and repeat the siege, which is how a lane lead becomes a map lead.
Headshot damage grows with critical strike chance, so if lane goes quiet you still come back into the game through items.
check: Whether their support or jungler has a way to close the gap on you, and where the wave is.
breaks: If you fall behind, stop stepping up to poke; stay behind your front line and use traps and the net to stay alive.

asks: how do I trade on Caitlyn
when do I poke in lane
how do I harass as Cait
should I be auto attacking them
say: Attack them each time they walk up for a minion, or just shove the wave if their support is looking for an engage.
more: They have to enter your range to last hit before you enter theirs, so every minion they want is a free shot for you.
Save the Headshot for a champion when you can: it comes every few attacks, so hit minions until it's loaded, then step up.
Shoving the wave is the safer version of the same plan; it pins them under tower where they lose minions and you can place traps.
check: Whether the Headshot is loaded, where their support is standing, and how many minions are between you.
breaks: If their jungler hasn't shown and your wave is far up, stop poking forward; back off to the middle of the lane.

asks: when is Caitlyn strong
what's my power spike on Cait
when do I get strong
which items matter on Caitlyn
say: You're strong early on range and again once crit items stack up, so press the lane now or play safer through the middle game.
more: Early, range alone wins trades; that edge fades as other champions buy items and gain ways to reach you.
Each crit item makes Headshot hit harder, because its bonus damage scales with critical strike chance.
Level six adds Ace in the Hole, a very long range finisher, but an enemy can step in front and take the bullet.
check: How many crit items you have compared with their marksman's item count.
breaks: If their team has several champions who can dive you, the mid game dip is deeper; stay grouped and buy for safety before more damage.

asks: what do I do in fights as Caitlyn
who do I shoot in teamfights
where do I stand as Cait
how do I teamfight on Caitlyn
say: Stay at max range hitting whoever's closest, or drop a trap under anyone your team locks down for a guaranteed Headshot.
more: A trapped or netted target takes an empowered Headshot, so any ally stun is a cue to put a trap under that champion.
Keep the net for the moment someone reaches you: it slows them and the recoil pushes you backward.
Before a fight starts, traps in the narrow paths around the objective make their engage awkward and protect your flank.
check: Who on their team can reach you, and whether their engage ability has already been used.
breaks: If a diver is already on top of you, forget damage; net away toward your support and rejoin from range.

when: their support is an engage champion
asks: how do I lane against a hook support
what do I do into an engage lane as Caitlyn
they keep all inning me
how do I play this lane on Cait
say: Stand behind your minions and poke only after their engage misses, or shove hard and trap around their tower so they can't walk up.
more: Most engage tools are stopped by minions or need them to walk at you, so a healthy wave between you is your shield.
The window after a missed engage is yours: they have nothing to threaten with for a while, so step up and take free attacks.
Holding your net for their engage instead of using it for damage is what keeps you alive at level two and three.
check: Whether their engage ability was just used, and whether your minion wave still covers you.
breaks: If they hit level two first, back off until you match it; a level lead is when engage lanes win outright.

asks: how do I play Fiora
what does Fiora want to do
what's my job as Fiora
how do I carry on Fiora
say: You're a duelist: win the one-on-one and push a side lane, or join a fight late from the side if their front line is already busy.
more: Hitting Vitals heals you and speeds you up, so long duels where you keep circling to the next Vital favor you.
A side lane you're winning forces them to send two people, and that's when your team can take an objective across the map.
You have no area damage or team crowd control, so standing in the middle of a five-on-five wastes what you're good at.
check: Who they send to stop you, and whether your team can hold four-on-four without you.
breaks: If your team can't survive without you, stay one lane away from the objective so you can still walk in.

asks: how do I trade on Fiora
when do I go in as Fiora
how do I win lane trades
should I fight him right now
say: Lunge onto a Vital that faces you and step back out, or hold the trade if the Vital sits on their far side.
more: A Vital hit gives health and move speed, so a short trade on a good Vital is nearly free and a trade on a bad one is not.
Bladework's second attack always crits, so Lunge, two quick attacks, then walk away is the full short trade.
Keep Riposte for their most important ability; if you spend it for damage, they get a window where you can't answer.
check: Which side the Vital is on, and whether they have already used their main crowd control.
breaks: If the wave is big and on their side, minion damage loses you the trade; wait until the wave thins or comes to you.

asks: when is Fiora strong
what's my spike on Fiora
when can I one v one
when do I start winning fights
say: Level six and your first finished item are the spikes; look for the full duel then, or keep short trades if their jungler is unseen.
more: Grand Challenge shows all four Vitals at once and speeds you up near the target, so one ultimate is a whole fight's worth of Vital hits.
Because Lunge applies on-hit effects, a finished item improves every part of your trade pattern at once.
You keep scaling in duels all game, so there's no need to force a coin-flip fight before these moments.
check: Whether your ultimate is ready and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If the enemy top is a level or an item ahead, the duel isn't yours yet; farm and trade only on easy Vitals.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Fiora
do I group or split
should I be with my team
where should I be right now
say: Push the side lane away from the next objective so they must answer you, or group if they can end the fight before you matter.
more: If one enemy comes, you duel them; if two come, your team has a numbers edge at the objective for as long as you stay alive.
The trade is a tower for an objective at worst, so push only as deep as you can get out of.
When you do join, come late and from the side onto one carry, with Riposte saved for the stun aimed at you.
check: How many enemies are missing from the map, and how long until the objective spawns.
breaks: If three or more are missing, they're coming for you; drop the wave and back off toward your own jungle.

when: the enemy top is a tank or has a stun
asks: how do I play against a tank as Fiora
what do I do into this lane
he has a stun how do I fight him
how do I beat this matchup
say: Bait out their stun and Riposte it to turn the fight, or keep to short Vital trades if you can't read the timing yet.
more: Riposte blocks the damage and the disable, and if it blocked an immobilizing effect its stab stuns them instead of slowing.
Against a tank the lane is slow; Vital hits wear them down over minutes rather than in one trade.
Later this matchup becomes the reason to split push, because one tank alone can't stop you from taking a tower.
check: Whether their stun has been used, and how their wind-up looks before they cast it.
breaks: If you Riposte early and miss the stun, back out at once; you have nothing left to answer their follow-up.

asks: how do I play Ivern
what is Ivern supposed to do
what does my champ want
how do I win as Ivern
say: You're a support in the jungle: make one carry strong with shields and roots, or use Daisy at objectives when no lane needs you.
more: You don't fight camps at all, so you stay healthy and can be in lanes far more often than a normal jungler.
You deal little damage yourself; every play needs an ally who can use the root, the shield or the brush.
Late game you stand with your best carry and keep them alive, with Daisy as a front line they have to deal with.
check: Which of your laners is strong enough to be worth playing around.
breaks: If your lanes are all losing, ganks won't fix it; keep groves going for gold and stay with whoever is still dealing damage.

asks: how do I clear on Ivern
what's my first clear as Ivern
where do I start on Ivern
how does Ivern jungle work
say: Set groves on the camps beside the lane you want, gank it while they grow, or plant your whole side first if nothing's gankable.
more: Camps can't hit you and you can't hit them; you start a grove, it grows over time, and you come back to free the monsters for gold and experience.
That means the clear is a route of visits, not fights, so plan to pass each camp twice with something useful in between.
You arrive at lanes with full health, so you lean toward ganking early more than almost any other jungler.
check: Whether the lane next to your groves is in a spot where a root would land.
breaks: If their jungler comes into your side while groves are growing, don't contest alone; plant on the other side and return later.

asks: who do I gank as Ivern
which lane should I help
where should I gank
which laner do I play around
say: Gank the lane with a melee champion who can dash to your root, or shield a ranged carry's lane if they just need safer trades.
more: When Rootcaller lands, your allies can dash to the rooted target, which gives a short-range laner an instant way in.
Triggerseed on the ally who goes in soaks the return damage and then bursts with a slow, which usually keeps the target in place.
You don't finish kills yourself, so pick the lane where your laner has the damage to end it.
check: Whether minions block the path of your root, and whether your laner has health to commit.
breaks: If the enemy laner has a dash ready, the root rarely lands; walk in close first or wait until they use it.

asks: when is Ivern strong
what's my power spike on Ivern
what do I do at six as Ivern
when should we fight
say: Level six brings Daisy: take a skirmish or dragon with her in front, or keep visiting lanes if she's on cooldown.
more: Daisy gives your team an extra body that fights for you, which matters most in small fights where one more front liner tips it.
You can re-cast to send her onto a target or pull her back, so point her at whoever your carry is hitting.
Your other spike is quieter: each time your carry finishes an item, your shield and brush are protecting more damage.
check: Whether Daisy is ready, and whether your nearest lane can walk to the fight first.
breaks: If the fight starts without Daisy, don't lead it; stand behind your carry and play for the root and shield only.

asks: what do I do in fights as Ivern
who do I shield
where do I stand as Ivern
how do I teamfight on Ivern
say: Stay beside your best carry with the shield and a brush under them, or shield your diver if that's who starts fights.
more: Brushmaker gives you and nearby allies bonus magic damage on attacks while in brush, so a brush under an attack-based carry is real damage.
The brush also hides them, which makes it harder for the enemy to start a fight on their terms.
Triggerseed on a melee ally who jumps in explodes on the people around them; on a carry it's a plain safety net.
check: Who on your team is dealing the damage this game, and who their team wants to jump on.
breaks: If their assassin is fed, forget the offensive shield; keep the root and shield for your carry and send Daisy at the assassin.

asks: how do I play Kayle
what does Kayle want
what's my job on Kayle
how do I win as Kayle
say: You're a late-game carry: farm safely now and take over fights later, or trade only when they waste a key ability on the wave.
more: Your passive improves as you level and put points into abilities, adding attack speed, move speed, range and waves of fire over time.
So the early game isn't about winning lane; it's about losing as little as possible on the way to those levels.
Late, you deal area damage from range and can make yourself or an ally invulnerable, which decides most teamfights.
check: How hard your lane opponent can punish you for walking up to a minion.
breaks: If your team is losing everywhere, farming alone won't hold; show up at fights near you once your ultimate is ready.

asks: how do I survive lane on Kayle
what's my plan early as Kayle
I'm weak early what do I do
do I just farm
say: Give up minions that cost health and farm near your tower, or step up when their jungler shows on the other side.
more: Experience matters more than gold early; standing in range of dying minions keeps your levels coming even when you can't last hit.
A wave held near your tower is hard to dive and easy for your jungler to cover, which is exactly the lane you want.
Each level you reach without dying brings the game closer to the point where the enemy has to end before you take over.
check: Where the wave is, and whether their jungler has been seen recently.
breaks: If they freeze the wave away from you, call your jungler to break it or look for experience elsewhere; don't walk into it.

asks: when is Kayle strong
what's my power spike on Kayle
when can I fight on Kayle
what levels matter on Kayle
say: Your spikes are six, eleven and sixteen, when your ultimate ranks up; trade more after each one, or keep farming if you're behind on items.
more: Your passive grows as you level, so each of those levels changes how you fight rather than just adding numbers.
Six also brings Divine Judgment, which makes you or an ally invulnerable for a moment and can turn a dive into a kill for you.
Attack speed and ability power items multiply what the passive gives, so a level spike with an item is the one to act on.
check: Your level against your lane opponent's, and whether your ultimate is ready.
breaks: If the enemy top is two levels up, the spike only brings you to even; keep farming until the next one.

asks: how do I trade on Kayle
can I fight him early
should I poke on Kayle
how do I lane as Kayle early
say: Poke with Radiant Blast when it lines up with minions and walk away, or skip trading entirely if they can run you down.
more: Radiant Blast slows and lowers resistances, so it's a safe way to chip from behind your wave without stepping into melee.
Starfire Spellblade's active hits harder on low-health targets, which makes it better for last hits and finishing than for opening.
Celestial Blessing heals you and speeds you up, so use it to leave a bad trade rather than to stay in one.
check: Your mana, since healing every poke runs you dry, and how much of the wave is on your side.
breaks: If you're out of mana or under half health, stop trading and recall on a pushed wave rather than staying exposed.

asks: what do I do in fights as Kayle
who do I ult on Kayle
where do I stand in teamfights
do I ult myself or a teammate
say: Hit their front line from behind yours and ult yourself when they dive you, or ult a fed ally if they're the one being focused.
more: Divine Judgment makes its target invulnerable and damages the area around them, so the best cast is on whoever is surrounded.
You deal area damage with your attacks late, so you don't need to reach their backline; the closest target is fine.
Their team will hold abilities for you, so let the fight start on someone else and walk in second.
check: Who their divers are and whether they've used their gap closers yet.
breaks: If you're caught before the fight with the ultimate down, the fight is lost; back off and trade an objective instead.

asks: how do I play Lulu
what does Lulu want
what's my job as Lulu
how do I support on Lulu
say: Pick one carry and keep them alive and fast, or poke in lane early while their support has no way to reach you.
more: Everything in your kit works on an ally: shield, attack speed and move speed, and an ultimate that gives health and knocks enemies up.
You have poke early through Pix and Glitterlance, so lane isn't passive, but you win games through someone else's damage.
The better your carry scales, the more your game does, so protecting their farm early is your long plan.
check: Which ally is strongest right now; it's not always your lane partner.
breaks: If your marksman is far behind, switch to whoever is carrying and follow them instead.

asks: how do I trade on Lulu
should I poke as Lulu
how do I harass in lane
when do I use my abilities in lane
say: Poke with Glitterlance when they step up for minions, or hold everything for defense if their support can engage on you.
more: Pix fires along with whoever he follows, and Glitterlance is cast from both you and Pix, so his position changes your poke angle.
Putting Pix on your marksman adds his bolts to their attacks and a shield, which wins even trades over time.
Whimsy on an enemy stops them attacking or casting, so against an all-in it's worth more than any poke you could do.
check: Your mana, and whether their engage ability is ready.
breaks: If their lane has kill pressure at level two or three, stop poking and stand where you can Whimsy whoever jumps in.

asks: when is Lulu strong
what's my spike on Lulu
what changes at six on Lulu
when can we fight in lane
say: Level six makes your lane hard to dive: fight back when they engage, or use Wild Growth early on your jungler's gank for the knock-up.
more: Wild Growth gives a large health boost and knocks up enemies around the ally, so the dive target suddenly becomes the trap.
Used on a melee ally who is already in the middle of them, it's an engage tool with a slow aura that follows.
Your item spikes are quiet ones: each support item strengthens your shields and buffs rather than you.
check: Whether your ultimate is ready, and whether their jungler is near your lane.
breaks: If you used the ultimate and it's down, the lane is diveable again; give ground until it's back.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Lulu
who do I ult as Lulu
who do I use Whimsy on
where do I stand in fights
say: Stand with your carry and Whimsy whoever dives them, or speed up your carry with it if nobody can reach them.
more: Whimsy has two uses and you get one per fight window, so decide before the fight which threat you're saving it for.
Wild Growth goes on the ally being focused; the knock-up interrupts the dive and the health buys time for your team.
Keep Pix on the ally who attacks the most, since his bolts fire each time they do.
check: Who their main diver is, and where that champion is standing before the fight.
breaks: If their damage comes from range instead of divers, don't hold Whimsy; use it for speed and attack speed right away.

when: their support is an engage champion
asks: how do I lane against an engage support as Lulu
they keep jumping on us
how do I play this lane
what do I do into a hook champ
say: Stay a step behind your marksman so only one of you gets caught, or push the wave fast if they can't engage through minions.
more: If they catch your marksman, you answer with Whimsy and a shield; if they catch you, your marksman has no protection at all.
A big wave on their side of the lane gives them fewer angles, and it gets you the level two timing first.
After six the matchup turns your way, because Wild Growth punishes exactly the kind of commit they want to make.
check: Whether minions cover you from their engage, and which of you is standing closer to them.
breaks: If you're both low and they still have their engage, don't hold the lane; recall and give up the wave.

asks: how do I play Nautilus
what does Nautilus want
what's my job as Naut
how do I support on Nautilus
say: You start fights: land Dredge Line or ult a carry so your team can follow, or peel with your root if your carry is the target.
more: Your kit is four ways to stop someone moving: hook, root on first attack, slow, and an ultimate that chases its target.
That makes you strong whenever your team is nearby to follow up and weak when you're alone or your team is too far back.
Later you're the front line as well, so buying tank items matters as much as landing hooks.
check: How close your team is, and whether they have the damage to finish what you start.
breaks: If your team is behind and can't follow, stop engaging; stand in front of your carry and lock down whoever comes in.

asks: how do I trade on Nautilus
when do I hook in lane
should I go in at level two
how do I lane as Naut
say: Look for a hook the moment you hit level two first, or just walk up and root with an attack if they stand too close.
more: Dredge Line pulls you and the target together, then your first attack roots them, so one hook is two crowd control effects in a row.
Titan's Wrath gives a shield and extra damage on attacks, so turn it on as you arrive rather than before.
A hook that hits terrain pulls you to the wall instead, which is also your way out if the trade goes badly.
check: Whether minions block the hook path, and whether your marksman is close enough to follow.
breaks: If you miss the hook, back off until it's ready; walking in without it just gets you poked down.

asks: when is Nautilus strong
what's my spike as Naut
what do I do at six on Nautilus
when can we all in
say: Six is your big spike: ult their marksman and follow with the hook for a kill, or roam mid with it if bot is pushed in.
more: Depth Charge chases its target and knocks up enemies along its path, so it lands without a skillshot.
Opening with the ultimate makes the hook easy, because the target is in the air when you throw it.
Reaching six before their support does gives you a short window where they can't match your all-in.
check: Whether your ultimate is ready, and how much health their marksman has.
breaks: If their support can shield or heal through your combo and your marksman is behind, save the ultimate for a gank instead.

asks: what do I do in fights as Nautilus
who do I ult on Naut
do I engage or peel
when do I go in
say: Ult their most dangerous carry to start the fight, or save it for the diver if your own carry is the one in danger.
more: An ultimate through their front line knocks up everyone it passes under, so the path matters as much as the target.
If you engage, you're gone from your backline; that's fine only when someone else can protect your carry.
Riptide's slow and your root on each new target let you hold two people in place once you're in the middle.
check: Where their carry is standing relative to their front line, and who is guarding your own carry.
breaks: If a hook pulls you onto their tank instead of a carry, don't follow through; walk back and peel.

asks: should I roam as Nautilus
can I go mid
when do I leave lane on Naut
should I help my jungler
say: Roam mid after your wave is pushed or your marksman recalls, or stay if leaving means your marksman gets dived.
more: Your crowd control needs no setup, so showing up in mid with a hook or ultimate usually forces Flash or a kill.
The cost is your marksman alone against two; that only works if the wave is safe or they're out of lane too.
A good roam also helps the next objective, because mid priority lets your jungler move first into the river.
check: Where your bot wave is, and whether the enemy mid is far enough up to reach.
breaks: If their bot lane is strong enough to dive under tower, stay; a kill mid won't pay for a lost tower and a dead marksman.

asks: how do I play Rakan
what does Rakan want
what's my job on Rakan
how do I support as Rakan
say: You dash in to start fights and dash back out to an ally, or play as a healer and shielder if going in isn't safe.
more: Grand Entrance knocks up where you land and Battle Dance flies you to an ally with a shield, so your engage has a built-in exit.
That exit needs an ally in range, which is why you stay close to teammates and never engage alone.
Gleaming Quill lets you heal allies after it hits a champion, so you still do a job on days when engaging is too risky.
check: Where your nearest ally is before you go in; that's your way back.
breaks: If your team is too far to follow or to dash back to, don't engage; poke with the quill and hold your dashes for peel.

asks: how do I trade on Rakan
when do I go in as Rakan
how do I lane on Rakan
should I engage in lane
say: Throw Gleaming Quill for poke and the heal, or go in with Grand Entrance when your marksman is close enough to dash back to.
more: The quill hitting a champion enables your heal, so landing it wins slow trades even if nothing else happens.
Going in and coming straight back out shields your marksman as you return, so a quick in-and-out trade is cheap.
Your passive shield comes back on its own over time, which lets you take a little poke between trades without real cost.
check: How far your marksman is behind you, and whether their support still has crowd control ready.
breaks: If their lane has a stun waiting for your dash, don't lead with it; poke and wait until they use that ability.

asks: when is Rakan strong
what's my spike on Rakan
what do I do at six as Rakan
when can I engage properly
say: Level six lets you run in and charm several people: start a fight at dragon with it, or roam mid if bot is quiet.
more: The Quickness gives you move speed and charms each enemy you touch, so it turns one knock-up into a chain of crowd control.
Combined with Grand Entrance you can lock down two or three people long enough for your team to arrive.
It's strongest in narrow river and jungle paths, where the enemy is forced to stand close together.
check: Whether your ultimate and Flash are ready, and whether enemies are bunched up.
breaks: If your team has no damage ready to follow, a big charm does nothing; use the speed to protect your carry instead.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Rakan
do I engage or stay back
who do I go on
how do I teamfight on Rakan
say: Run in with The Quickness and knock up their carries, then dash back, or stay with your carry and shield them if they're diving.
more: After the engage, Battle Dance takes you to an ally and can be cast again briefly, so you can shield two teammates on the way out.
The best engage angle is from the side or from fog, since a straight run at them gives time to react.

Knuckle Down's two attacks deal damage based on the target's max health and give move speed toward them, which starts most trades.
Facebreaker stuns only if enemies are on both sides of you, so with minions behind you and them in front it's a stun, not a slow.
